findings.quote: for 45 s or until a front door is opened
findings.explanation: Allowed movement time after ignition off is 45 s here but 60 s in WLC-023. Both cannot be true, and WLC-023 also lacks the door-open condition.
findings.rewrite: After ignition off, the controller shall allow window movement for [TBD: confirm 45 s or 60 s] or until a front door is opened, whichever comes first.

findings.explanation: 'End position' is used in the express mode definition but is not defined as a position. Also no time limit is given for stopping the motor, unlike the other stop requirements.
findings.rewrite: The motor shall be stopped within [TBD: stop time] when the window reaches fully open (480 mm) or fully closed (0 mm).

findings.explanation: 'Quickly' is not measurable. The requirement also does not say how soon after the rain report the closing must start, or whether anti-pinch stays active.
findings.rewrite: When the rain sensor reports rain, the window shall close fully within [TBD: closing time] of the report.

findings.quote: shall be active in manual mode and in express mode
findings.explanation: This requires anti-pinch protection in manual mode without qualification. WLC-017 disables it when the controller is not normalized, and manual mode is possible in that state.
findings.rewrite: When the controller is normalized, anti-pinch protection shall be active in manual mode and in express mode.

findings.quote: shall be disabled when the controller is not normalized
findings.explanation: This contradicts WLC-016, which makes anti-pinch active in manual mode with no normalization condition. Disabling a safety function also needs a rationale and a check of the safety impact.
findings.rewrite: Anti-pinch protection shall be disabled when the controller is not normalized [TBD: confirm with safety analysis and align with WLC-016].

findings.explanation: 'Robust' and 'all disturbances' cannot be verified, because no test can cover every disturbance.
findings.rewrite: The anti-pinch function shall not trigger a false pinch detection under [TBD: list of disturbances, e.g. supply voltage ripple, road vibration, door slam] and shall still detect a pinch above 100 N.

findings.explanation: This gives 60 s of movement after ignition off, but WLC-007 gives 45 s. It also leaves out the front-door-open condition, so it partly duplicates WLC-007.
findings.rewrite: Delete WLC-023 and keep WLC-007 with the confirmed time value.

findings.quote: exceeds the limit, the controller shall reduce motor current to a safe value
findings.explanation: Neither the temperature limit nor the reduced current value is given, so no test can check it. WLC-026 uses 140 °C, and it is unclear how the two relate.
findings.rewrite: When the estimated motor temperature exceeds [TBD: temperature limit, below 140 °C], the controller shall limit motor current to [TBD: reduced current value] A.

findings.quote: shall store diagnostic trouble code B1A01 when the Hall sensor signal is missing for more than 200 ms while the motor is driven, and shall stop the motor
findings.explanation: Storing the DTC and stopping the motor are separate behaviors and need separate tests. The motor stop also has no time limit.
findings.rewrite: WLC-029a: The controller shall store DTC B1A01 when the Hall sensor signal is missing for more than 200 ms while the motor is driven. WLC-029b: The controller shall stop the motor within [TBD: stop time] after storing B1A01.

findings.quote: shall store diagnostic trouble code B1A02 when motor current exceeds 25 A for more than 50 ms and shall stop the motor and shall set the fault state in WLC_Status
findings.explanation: Three separate behaviors (store DTC, stop motor, set CAN fault state) are combined in one requirement. The motor stop also has no time limit.
findings.rewrite: WLC-030a: The controller shall store DTC B1A02 when motor current exceeds 25 A for more than 50 ms. WLC-030b: The controller shall stop the motor within [TBD: stop time] when B1A02 is stored. WLC-030c: The controller shall set the fault state in WLC_Status when B1A02 is stored.

findings.quote: In sleep mode, the controller shall draw less than 100 µA from the 12 V supply.
findings.explanation: This is word for word the same as WLC-004.
'User friendly' is subjective and has no measurable criterion, so it could also be called untestable.
findings.rewrite: [TBD: measurable usability criteria, e.g. switch feedback or response time to a switch press]

findings.quote: The software shall be developed according to the company software process.
findings.explanation: This describes how the software is developed, not what the product does. It belongs in a project plan or quality plan.
findings.rewrite: Move to the project or quality plan. If a product requirement is needed, name the standard, e.g. [TBD: required software standard and integrity level].
